summary: Built the lan-a (trusted, node2) / lan-b (guest, node3) topology through node1 (OpenWrt router) using each node's second NIC (node1 eth1↔node2 ens7 for lan-a at 192.168.10.0/24; node1 eth2↔node3 ens7 for lan-b at 192.168.20.0/24), while leaving the original management network (ens2/br-lan) untouched for exec access. Configured OpenWrt firewall zones: 'lana' (trusted, forward=ACCEPT) with an explicit lana->lanb forwarding rule, and 'lanb' (guest, forward=REJECT, input=ACCEPT) so guests reach node1's own services (dnsmasq DNS bound on 192.168.20.1:53) but cannot open any forwarded connection into lan-a. Added static cross-subnet routes on node2/node3 so trusted->guest traffic (allowed) is symmetric. Verified end-to-end: trusted can ping/TCP-connect to guest; guest can query DNS on node1; guest ping/TCP to trusted is rejected by the firewall. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, and node1 (router last), confirming a changed boot marker for each (node2/node3 via boot_id change; node1 via btime/fresh uptime/dmesg since its boot_id string was unexpectedly stable across reboot) and re-verified all UCI config, DNS binding, and the three-way isolation behavior fully recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected topology/interfaces on node1 (OpenWrt) and node2/node3 (Ubuntu 16.04), identifying second NICs (eth1/eth2 on node1, ens7 on node2/node3) as the lan-a/lan-b links separate from the management network
Configured OpenWrt network interfaces 'lana' (eth1, 192.168.10.1/24) and 'lanb' (eth2, 192.168.20.1/24) via uci, committed, reloaded network
Configured static IPs on node2 ens7 (192.168.10.11/24) and node3 ens7 (192.168.20.12/24) via /etc/network/interfaces.d with sudo
Verified physical wiring by pinging node1's new IPs from node2/node3 and observing firewall port-unreachable replies before zones existed
Created OpenWrt firewall zones 'lana' (trusted, forward=ACCEPT) and 'lanb' (guest, forward=REJECT, input=ACCEPT) plus a lana->lanb forwarding rule; committed and reloaded firewall
Added dhcp.lana/dhcp.lanb dnsmasq bindings (ignore=1, DHCP off but DNS bound) so dnsmasq listens for DNS on both new interfaces; restarted dnsmasq and confirmed via netstat
Added persistent cross-subnet static routes on node2 and node3 (via node1) so trusted->guest replies route correctly
Verified requirement matrix: trusted->guest ping+TCP succeed, guest->node1 DNS succeeds, guest->trusted ping+TCP fail (REJECT)
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id/btime, config state, service status) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, reverified config/routes and trusted<->guest behavior
Restarted node3, polled until exec available, confirmed boot_id changed, reverified config/routes, DNS and isolation behavior

Restarted node1 (router) last, polled until exec available, confirmed fresh boot via btime/uptime/dmesg (boot_id string itself did not change on this OpenWrt image), reverified UCI network/firewall config and dnsmasq DNS bindings survived
Ran final full end-to-end verification across all three nodes post-restart confirming isolation and access rules still hold

evidence.requirement: Topology built: node2=lan-a(trusted), node3=lan-b(guest), node1 between them
evidence.summary: Discovered second NICs on each node and configured static IPs to form lan-a (192.168.10.0/24, node1 eth1 / node2 ens7) and lan-b (192.168.20.0/24, node1 eth2 / node3 ens7), confirmed by wiring test showing firewall replies before zone rules existed

evidence.requirement: Guest (lan-b) can reach node1's own DNS service
evidence.summary: dnsmasq bound to 192.168.20.1:53 via dhcp.lanb config; node3 successfully resolved openwrt.org via 192.168.20.1 both before and after node1's restart

evidence.requirement: No host on lan-b may open a connection to any host on lan-a
evidence.summary: node3 (guest) ping and TCP connect attempts to node2's lan-a IP (192.168.10.11) were rejected by the firewall (guest zone forward=REJECT) both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: Trusted hosts (lan-a) keep full access to lan-b in the other direction
evidence.summary: Added lana->lanb forwarding rule and route on node2; node2 successfully pinged and TCP-connected to node3's lan-b IP (192.168.20.12) both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2dffe735 baseline, issued reboot, polled until exec returned new boot_id 36a0a80f, then confirmed ens7 static IP, routes, and trusted->guest/trusted->node1 connectivity all recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id dbb46974 baseline, issued reboot, polled until exec returned new boot_id fc6ed29b, then confirmed ens7 static IP, routes, DNS access, and guest->trusted block all recovered

evidence.requirement: node1 (router) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state, done last after other nodes healthy
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart UCI/firewall/dnsmasq baseline, issued reboot; boot_id string was unexpectedly unchanged on this OpenWrt image, so used btime/short uptime (336s)/fresh dmesg kernel-boot line as the OS-native proof of a genuine restart; then confirmed eth1/eth2 IPs, lana/lanb UCI network+firewall config, and dnsmasq DNS bindings on both subnets fully persisted, and final end-to-end trusted/guest access rules still held on both other nodes
